key_insight: IQ-JEPA uses self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled ultrasound IQ data to learn phase-aware representations that dramatically improve sound-speed and attenuation estimation with far fewer labels.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the cost and labeling burden of quantitative ultrasound, making faster and more scalable tissue property estimation more practical for real imaging systems.
method: Pretrain a joint-embedding predictor to reconstruct masked IQ latent regions from visible context.
Use a Hermitian vision transformer that processes complex IQ data directly with phase-equivariant attention and phase-invariant conjugate-product features.
Fine-tune the pretrained encoder on simulated sound-speed maps and test transfer to attenuation and cross-distribution settings.
evidence_signal: On 79,293 Fullwave 2.5 simulations, pretraining on 63,435 unlabeled acquisitions achieved 15.60 m/s error at 10,000 labels and 8.71 m/s at full labels, with gains growing as labels decreased.
watch_item: Performance depends on simulation-to-real transfer and the quality of unlabeled pretraining data, so generalization outside the studied phantom distributions may require further validation.
paper_title: IQ-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture with a Hermitian Vision Transformer for Sound Speed and Attenuation Estimation from Ultrasound IQ Data
